title: Philly Cheesesteak
subtitle: Thinly sliced beef with peppers, onion, and melted cheese in a hoagie roll
excerpt: Shaved beef cooked fast with onions and green pepper, then piled into a soft roll and covered with melted cheese. Messy and very filling.
sourceNotes: A street food staple from the US city, first sold in the 1930s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Slice the beef and refrigerate for up to one day. Cook everything to order.

content.text: Thin beef is the key. Freeze the steak for 30 minutes so it firms up enough to slice paper-thin. Cook on the highest heat you have so the meat gets colour fast rather than steaming.

items.prepNote: frozen for 30 minutes then shaved as thin as possible

content.text: Place the ribeye in the freezer for 30 minutes. Slice as thinly as possible across the grain. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat half the oil in the skillet over a high heat until smoking. Add the onion and pepper. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until softened and lightly charred. Push to one side.
Add the remaining oil to the empty side of the pan. Lay the beef in one layer. Do not stir. Let it sear for 1 minute.
Chop through the beef with the edge of the spatula into rough pieces. Stir and toss with the vegetables.
Divide the mixture into two mounds in the pan. Lay cheese slices over each mound and lower the heat. Let the cheese melt for 1 minute.
Split the rolls and warm them in a dry pan cut-side down for 1 minute. Slide a mound into each roll and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The beef steams rather than sears.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, or too much meat was added at once.
items.fix: Get the pan smoking before adding the beef and cook in two batches if needed.

items.symptom: The beef is tough and chewy.
items.cause: It was sliced too thick or cut with the grain.
items.fix: Freeze the steak longer and always slice across the grain for shorter muscle fibres.

items.symptom: The cheese does not melt evenly.
items.cause: The heat was left on high when the cheese was added.
items.fix: Lower to medium and cover the pan with a lid or piece of foil for 60 seconds.
